arxiv-2302-11081.description: Abstract The data management of large companies often prioritize more recent data, as a source of higher accuracy prediction than outdated data. For example, the Facebook data policy retains user search histories for 6 6 months while the Google data retention policy states that browser information may be stored for up to 9 9 months.

arxiv-2305-11671.title: Search for vector dark matter in microwave cavities with Rydberg atoms
arxiv-2305-11671.creator: Jordan Gué, Aurélien Hees, Jérôme Lodewyck, Rodolphe Le Targat, Peter Wolf
arxiv-2305-11671.description: Abstract We propose a novel experiment to search for dark matter, based on the application of an electric field inside a microwave cavity and electrometry using Rydberg atoms. We show that this kind of experiment could be extremely useful for detecting specific dark matter candidates, namely massive vector fields coupled to the photon field, more commonly known as dark photons.

arxiv-2307-15736.title: Hunting Nonstandard Neutrino Interactions and Leptoquarks in Dark Matter Experiments Preprint: KEK-QUP-2023-0007, KEK-TH-2516, KEK-Cosmo-0309, IPMU23-0009
arxiv-2307-15736.creator: Thomas Schwemberger, Volodymyr Takhistov, Tien-Tien Yu
arxiv-2307-15736.description: Abstract Next generation direct dark matter (DM) detection experiments will have unprecedented capabilities to explore coherent neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE ν \nu NS) complementary to dedicated neutrino experiments. We demonstrate that future DM experiments can effectively probe nonstandard neutrino interactions (NSI) mediated by scalar fields in the scattering of solar and atmospheric neutrinos.

arxiv-2505-06291.title: ALFEE: Adaptive Large Foundation Model for EEG Representation
arxiv-2505-06291.creator: Wei Xiong, Junming Lin, Jiangtong Li, Jie Li, Changjun Jiang
arxiv-2505-06291.description: Abstract . While foundation models excel in text, image, and video domains, the critical biological signals, particularly electroencephalography (EEG), remain underexplored. EEG benefits neurological research with its high temporal resolution, operational practicality, and safety profile. However, low signal-to-noise ratio, inter-subject variability, and cross-paradigm differences hinder the generalization of current models.

arxiv-2508-21165.title: Data-Driven Bifurcation Handling in Physics-Based Reduced-Order Vascular Hemodynamic Models
arxiv-2508-21165.creator: Natalia L. Rubio, Eric F. Darve, Alison L. Marsden
arxiv-2508-21165.description: Abstract Background and Objective: Three-dimensional (3D) computational fluid dynamics simulations of cardiovascular flows provide high-fidelity hemodynamic predictions to support cardiovascular medicine, but require substantial computational resources, limiting their clinical applicability. Reduced-order models (ROMs) offer computationally efficient alternatives but suffer from significant accuracy losses, particularly at vessel bifurcations where complex flow physics are inadequately captured by standard Poiseuille flow assumptions.

arxiv-2510-26761.title: “Enough” Wigner negativity implies genuine multipartite entanglement
arxiv-2510-26761.creator: Lin Htoo Zaw, Jiajie Guo, Qiongyi He, Matteo Fadel, Shuheng Liu
arxiv-2510-26761.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lin Htoo Zaw, Jiajie Guo, Qiongyi He, Matteo Fadel, Shuheng Liu. Wigner negativity and genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) are key nonclassical resources that enable computational advantages and broader quantum-information tasks. In this work, we prove two theorems for multimode continuous-variable systems that relate these nonclassical resources. Both theorems show that “enough” Wigner negativity—either a large-enough Wigner negativity volume along a suitably-chosen two-dimensional slice, or a large-enough nonclassicality depth of the centre-of-mass of a system—certifies the presence of GME.
